target_customer: B2B revenue operations, account management and product led sales teams with data in a warehouse
problem: Account teams lack timely signals from customer data, so churn and expansion opportunities are missed. Workbase turns warehouse data into dashboards, checklists and triggered workflows.
product_category: Data activation and revenue operations workflow tool

founders.name: John Tan
founders.background_notes: YC page and the Hightouch post name him co-founder and CEO. A Quild newsletter summary says he previously worked at Segment; not opened, so not recorded as an employer.

founders.name: Ed Parsons
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has built things with computers since age 12.

technical_complexity.rationale: Warehouse connectors, a formula engine and event triggers are standard but demanding data engineering for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow automation on top of a warehouse was easy for data activation vendors to build, which is what Hightouch described doing itself.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Hightouch acquired Workbase in April 2022 because it was missing workflow automation as it moved beyond reverse ETL.

market_need_then: Companies were moving customer data into warehouses and wanted to act on it; Workbase's own pitch claimed proactive account management raises net retained revenue by up to 20 percent, a company claim.

branding.domain_note: The YC listing had no website. workbase.com now belongs to an unrelated Polish company called Workbase.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic name shared with several other companies (Workerbase, an unrelated Workbase in Poland), and no brand coverage was found.

outcome_analysis: Workbase was a two founder team that built workflow automation on warehouse data and was bought by Hightouch in April 2022, ten months after a Summer 2020 batch. Hightouch's own post says it acquired Workbase to fill a feature gap, and reports 400 plus users and 1 billion records synced daily, pointing to a capability acquisition rather than a large business. Terms and funding are not public.
notes: Funding: CB Insights lists 130 thousand dollars over 3 rounds with Y Combinator and Felicis as investors, but a second CB Insights page shows a different investor; unverified, no round recorded. Product page now at workbase.com is an unrelated company. YC page mentions the founders saw internal tools at Segment but gives no employer data for the founders. Competitor list empty because no dated 2020 source was found. Acquisition described as acquihire like because the stated rationale was a missing feature; terms undisclosed.
